title: Fix "Upstream already exists" when creating a fork
body:
Fixes #160377

### Problem

When a push is rejected because the user has no write access, the GitHub extension offers to create a fork. That flow hardcodes the remote names it wants to use:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/github/src/pushErrorHandler.ts#L223-L229

```ts
// Issue: what if there's already an `upstream` repo?
await repository.renameRemote(remote.name, 'upstream');

// Issue: what if there's already another `origin` repo?
await repository.addRemote('origin', remoteUrl);
```

If the repository already has a remote named `upstream` — the usual setup when you cloned a fork, and the case reported in #160377 (and the duplicate #189101) — `git remote rename` fails with `remote upstream already exists` and the whole fork flow is aborted. The same applies to `addRemote('origin', ...)` when the rejected remote was not named `origin` and an `origin` remote already exists.

### Change

Added `getUniqueRemoteName()` to `extensions/github/src/util.ts`, which falls back to a suffixed name (`upstream-1`, `origin-1`, …) when the preferred name is taken, and used it in `handlePermissionDeniedError`. The names are computed once, before the rename, from the remote list adjusted for the pending rename, so the result does not depend on `repository.state.remotes` having refreshed in between. The subsequent `fetch` / `setBranchUpstream` / `push` / `setConfig` calls use those names instead of the hardcoded strings.

The `origin` = fork, `upstream` = original semantics are unchanged, and no existing remote is removed or overwritten.

### Behaviour

| remotes before | rejected remote | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin` | `origin` | `upstream`, `origin` (unchanged from today) |
| `origin`, `upstream` | `origin` | `upstream-1`, `origin` |
| `gh`, `origin` | `gh` | `upstream`, `origin-1` |

### Testing

`tsc --noEmit` is clean for `extensions/github`, and two unit tests for `getUniqueRemoteName` were added to `extensions/github/src/test/github.test.ts`.

title: mcp: support remote URL variables
body:
## Summary

- Support declared URL variables when installing remote MCP servers, including Dynatrace-style environment URLs.
- Preserve fixed variable values, including empty strings, without creating unnecessary prompts.
- Reject conflicting URL/header input definitions instead of discarding defaults, choices, or secret metadata.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

The MCP Registry's `2025-12-11` schema allows remote transports to declare their own URL variables. The existing converter handled variables inside headers and arguments but copied remote URLs unchanged. A manifest such as the [Dynatrace server manifest](https://github.com/Dynatrace/dynatrace-for-ai/blob/main/server.json) therefore left its environment placeholder unresolved in the generated configuration.

### Implementation

Remote transport types now expose the URL-variable map separately from package transports. Shared normalization replaces each declared placeholder with its explicit fixed value or a VS Code input reference. The same transformation is used for URL, header, environment, and argument conversion, and for registry-only URL matching.

Fixed-value declarations do not generate interactive inputs. Equivalent URL/header input definitions are deduplicated; incompatible definitions throw a localized error that propagates through existing installation error handling. In particular, a non-secret URL definition cannot silently override a secret header input with the same ID.

### Behavior and constraints

- SSE and streamable HTTP share the conversion path and continue using the existing runtime configuration resolver.
- An explicit empty value remains empty, while a default still belongs to a configurable input.
- Replacement processes every occurrence in one pass. Declared names are escaped for literal matching, replacement text is not recursively interpreted, and undeclared placeholders remain unchanged.
- Registry-only access still requires exact equality with the original URL or its converted representation. This does not introduce wildcard URL matching or permit replacing a declared fixed value with a prompt.
- Fixed values are scoped to their originating declaration and do not enter the shared interactive-input namespace.
- This adds URL-variable support rather than claiming complete support for every field in the newer registry schema. Existing runtime resolution, transport selection, and input persistence remain unchanged.

</details>

title: Auto mode: support server-owned Hydra-RL multi-turn routing
body:
## Summary

Add VS Code client support for the server-owned Hydra-RL multi-turn protocol on the current `POST /auto` path.

- Advertise `hydra_rl_multi_turn` capability whenever routing reaches `/auto`, without a second client rollout flag. Activate local scheduling only when CAPI returns valid controller state; control and older servers keep sticky Auto behavior.
- Keep the opaque controller token and a bounded skip budget in the existing conversation cache. Honor exactly the authorized number of subsequent user turns, then use the server's selected model. The client does not implement model ranking, drift, or upgrade policy.
- Count distinct chat request IDs rather than prompt text or endpoint resolutions. Serialize identified turns, deduplicate repeated resolutions, and send `advance: false` for ancillary calls and renewals. Expiry inside a skip window cannot refill the consumed budget.
- Reset applicable state on compaction, authentication changes, disposal/eviction, tier or incompatible vision changes, and leaving or falling back from Auto. Typed model rejections invalidate active Hydra selections without retrying the model call or falling back to a rejected endpoint.
- Recover once without state after a state-bearing `/auto` request is rejected with HTTP 400. Preserve compatible cached state across transient routing errors, and guard in-flight invalidation/account races.
- Record server activation and authorized skips on `automode.autoV2Decision`, plus a per-user-turn `automode.hydraRlMultiTurnSkip` event. Opaque controller and model-session tokens are not logged.

## Protocol And Rollout

This implements the merged server contract in github/copilot-api#37326 and follows the runtime transport in github/copilot-agent-runtime#17183. Related VS Code routing work: #324613.

The implementation targets current `main`; it does not depend on or port the older client-owned capability-drift state machine from #324613. `skip_turns` is validated as an integer in `[0, 7]`, matching the merged runtime contract. Server decision labels are not interpreted by the client.

CAPI remains the only experiment assignment point. This PR enables protocol support, not the production experiment. Prompt/history preparation is unchanged. This is an experimental efficiency treatment, not a claim of improved answer quality.

Client protocol and lifecycle details are documented in `extensions/copilot/docs/auto-mode/hydra-rl-multi-turn-routing.md`.

title: agentHost: recreate provisional drafts after reinitialization
body:
## Summary

- announce when an Agent Host reconnect falls back to a fresh initialize because the host forgot the client
- detach provisional draft subscriptions before that initialize snapshots subscriptions, then recreate those drafts after reinitialization
- preserve ordinary replay reconnects, materialized-session restore, and full remote connection replacement behavior

## Problem

Selecting Claude in the new-session composer eagerly creates a provisional backend session without downloading the Claude SDK. If the Agent Host restarts while that draft is selected, the client previously replayed the draft subscription into the fresh host. The host treated the unknown URI as a materialized session restore, called Claude's restore path, and downloaded the SDK even though the user had not clicked **Download** or sent a message.

Reproduction:

1. Remove the Claude SDK cache and Claude download consent.
2. Select Claude in the new-session composer without clicking **Download** or sending a message.
3. Restart the Agent Host.
4. Observe a lazy Claude SDK download (`explicit=false`) and newly persisted download consent.

## Fix

The protocol client now exposes a reinitialization lifecycle only for the state-loss boundary (`reconnect` returns `AHP NotFound`, requiring a fresh `initialize`). Before the fresh initialize payload is assembled, the sessions provider releases its client-owned provisional draft subscriptions and cancels any in-flight eager create. After reinitialization completes, it reissues the normal draft `createSession` flow.

Materialized session subscriptions remain active and are still restored normally, including a cold SDK download when required. A successful replay reconnect to a host that retained state does not recreate drafts.

title: agentHost: Track subagent progress from task status
body:
## Summary

Track every Copilot subagent turn from the runtime task registry instead of inferring completion from stop hooks or SDK `subagent.completed` events.

- subscribe to `session.background_tasks_changed` and reconcile `session.rpc.tasks.list()`
- complete initial, synchronous, background, and retained follow-up turns when their agent task becomes idle, completed, failed, or cancelled
- serialize task-status reads and reject stale session-wide snapshots
- keep `subagent.completed`, `subagent.failed`, and stop hooks for observability only
- add deterministic E2E coverage for a retained background child completing its initial turn and two successive `write_agent` follow-ups

## Why

The SDK emits `subagent.completed` for the original task invocation, but not after a retained subagent processes a `write_agent` follow-up. Stop hooks can also finish before final assistant events, so neither event is a reliable turn-completion boundary.

The task registry exposes the lifecycle for both synchronous and background subagents as `running` → `idle`, including every follow-up, and provides the stable `agentId` and parent `toolCallId`. Live validation against the pinned CLI confirmed that synchronous and retained subagents both publish these transitions. This is a follow-up to #334781.

## E2E coverage

The Copilot E2E suite now covers:

- synchronous custom-subagent completion, including definitions without display names or explicit tool lists
- retained background-subagent initial completion
- two successive follow-ups to the same retained child
- exact child responses and complete child-turn state with no active turn after each invocation
- child tool routing and parent/child transcript separation
- session reopen and subagent transcript restoration

The new three-round AHP snapshot verifies that each follow-up produces `chat/turnStarted`, the child response, and exactly one `chat/turnComplete`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`

title: nes: refactor: remove unshipped joint completion provider
body:
## Summary

Remove the joint inline completion provider, which never shipped, together with the configuration, registration indirection, and request-context overrides introduced to support it. Preserve the shipped NES and ghost-text completion paths.

## Changes

- Delete `jointInlineCompletionProvider.ts`, its strategy enums, and its three experiment settings.
- Register `InlineEditProviderFeatureContribution` and `CompletionsCoreContribution` directly instead of routing their activation through the joint-provider contribution.
- Fold the separately extracted NES feature object back into its contribution. Scope the inline completion provider's disposal to its registration lifetime.
- Remove exports used only by the joint provider, undefined callback placeholders, and the joint-only cursor-at-end-of-line helper.
- Remove `enforceCacheDelay` from the NES request context and all callers. Tests and simulations use the existing delay configuration rather than a production request-context bypass.
- Extract the shared Learn More command and URL constants into a feature-independent module to avoid an import-order regression from direct contribution registration.

## Why remove `enforceCacheDelay`?

The joint provider normally preferred ghost-text completions but had a fast path to keep an already-shown NES. It gave NES **10 ms** to return an equivalent cached suggestion before starting a competing ghost-text request.

The ordinary minimum response delay could cause an immediately available cached result to miss that window. The joint provider therefore disabled delay enforcement when the document version had not changed, and retained it when the document had changed. A later strategy also bypassed the delay when selecting NES directly.

This flag was not a cache-validity check. Setting it to `false` bypassed the entire minimum-response-delay calculation. The regular VS Code NES entry point already defaulted it to `true`, and the library entry point explicitly supplied `true`; the joint provider was the production caller that needed the override.

Removing the joint provider removes that need. This PR deletes the override, **not the normal response-delay logic**: general, rebased, subsequent, and speculative delays remain, including subtraction of time already spent handling the request. Cache lookup, rebasing, rejection filtering, and cancellation handling are unchanged. `NESInlineCompletionContext` remains for its typed NES change hint.

The simulation runner resolves all services, including its optional runtime, before awaiting the delay configuration update. This respects the synchronous lifetime of `ServicesAccessor` while keeping simulations free of artificial waiting.

The completions provider service is deliberately retained because its shared instantiation context also supplies NES neighbor-file context.

## Learn More initialization

Direct contribution registration reverses an existing circular import: the feature imports the completion provider, while the provider imported the feature's command and URL constants. The provider's module-level Learn More action could consequently capture undefined values before the feature initialized those constants.

Both consumers now import the constants from `common/inlineEditCommands.ts`, eliminating that dependency cycle. A before/after in-memory build of the actual feature entry reproduces the broken initialization order without the extraction and verifies the corrected order with it.

## Validation

- Focused Vitest run: **70 passed, 2 skipped**, covering:
  - NES caching.
  - Speculative requests and response delays, including a new fake-timer regression test for ordinary minimum response delay.
  - Model configuration resolution.
  - Configuration service behavior.
- Copilot extension TypeScript project: passed.
- Actual feature-entry bundle initialization check, before and after the constants extraction: passed.
- Targeted ESLint for the simulation runner, including the accessor-after-await rule: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

title: Document the UI composition ownership heuristic
body:
## Predictable UI composition — 2 of 3: candidate authoring guidance

Stack:

1. **#335345 — shared composition token foundation**
2. **#335346 — ownership guidance (this PR)**
3. **#335350 — `WorkbenchButtonBar` pilot**

## Proposed guidance

Use **one relationship, one owner** as a review heuristic:

- Put a relationship in the lowest component contract that understands all participating elements.
- Treat ownership as responsibility, not as the location of the CSS declaration.
- Keep primitive content neutral about unknown neighbors.
- Let a rendered icon own size/fitting, a control own internal relationships, and a parent own relationships between controls—unless the actual composition provides a better boundary.
- Choose `gap`, padding, or a pair-specific margin according to the relationship; no mechanism is inherently correct.

The design-philosophy wording explicitly marks this as candidate guidance, not settled doctrine or an automatic lint rule.

## Prior-art and scope check

`IconLabel` is relevant prior art: `Button` already shares its lower-level inline-icon renderer, while the full widget has different resource/list-label semantics. This guidance and the active pilot therefore do not require embedding it or adding a new `IconLabel` API.

Mutable size-token IDs and values are sourced from `baseSizes.ts`; theme colors remain governed by their separate color registries. Broader instruction/skill source-of-truth consolidation remains tracked in #335370; this PR only avoids duplicating the spacing values it changes.

title: agentHost: serialize replacement turns after abort
body:
## Summary

- start Copilot aborts immediately so cancellation can bypass blocked chat work
- insert abort settlement into the existing per-chat sequencer so replacement turns cannot overtake it
- add focused coverage for the abort/replacement ordering

## Root cause

The Agent Host applied `chat/turnCancelled` synchronously but invoked the provider abort asynchronously. A client could therefore send a replacement turn after observing cancellation while the Copilot runtime was still aborting the previous turn. In `src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts`, the JSDoc for `TextEditor.viewColumn` states:

/**

title: Terminal: tolerate float error when scaling charHeight to device pixels
body:
`getXtermScaledDimensions` ceils `font.charHeight * devicePixelRatio`. `charHeight` is xterm's device cell height divided by `devicePixelRatio` (`getFont` reads `renderService.dimensions.css.cell`), so the product can land a few ulps above the whole pixel and ceil adds a device pixel per row.

At `window.zoomLevel: 1` (ratio 1.2) with a 22 px cell, `22 / 1.2 * 1.2` is `22.000000000000004`, so rows are computed with 23 px. A 1257 px tall terminal editor gets 54 rows instead of 57, and since the grid is bottom-anchored the three missing rows appear as blank space above the first line. 25 px and 28 px cells hit the same case.

Fix: subtract a small tolerance before the ceil. Fractional device heights (e.g. 17 * 1.2 = 20.4) still round up.

Adds unit tests for both cases.

title: automations: fix: keep popup Escape from closing the dialog
body:
Fixes #334869.

## Problem

Escape should dismiss an Automation picker and leave the modal and unsaved form intact. The custom SelectBox closes on keydown and returns focus to its select, whereas the generic Dialog closes on keyup.

The existing Automations keyboard guard cleared popup ownership on every keydown outside a popup and every unrelated keyup. Holding Escape therefore produced this sequence:

1. Escape keydown targets the popup and enables suppression.
2. The popup closes and restores focus to the select.
3. Repeated Escape keydown targets the form and clears suppression.
4. Escape keyup reaches Dialog and closes the modal too.

Interleaved keydown/keyup events can cause the same failure. An ordinary `keyboard.press("Escape")` passes on the original code; repeated keydowns reliably reproduce the double dismissal.

## Fix

Establish popup ownership on the initial, non-repeated Escape keydown and retain it until Escape keyup. Ignore repeat and unrelated key events when updating that ownership. A fresh independent Escape press still closes the dialog.

The change stays in the Automations keyboard helper. Shared Dialog and SelectBox implementations, popup detection, focus trapping, listener registration/disposal, and native-picker selection are unchanged.

## Regression coverage

Four composed tests use real Dialog, SelectBox and ContextViewHandler instances, with the production listener registration order and events dispatched to the actual focused element. They cover normal Escape, key repeat, interleaved keydown and interleaved keyup. Each verifies popup dismissal, focus restoration, preserved selection and dismissal by a subsequent independent Escape.

Three new regression cases fail against the original helper.

## Validation

- 51 tests pass across Automation dialog, Dialog and SelectBox suites.
- Changed-file ESLint, whitespace checks and commit hygiene pass.
- Live macOS Agents-window checks reproduce the failure before the fix and pass afterward for Schedule repeat/interleaved keys, Time repeat and Day repeat. They also verify unsaved name preservation and normal subsequent dismissal.
- A live held-Escape check also passes for the workspace action popup.

Native OS pickers, Windows/Linux, screen readers and physical keyboard timing were not certified by this validation.

body:
add some diagnostic information to the response telemetry to collect more information about missing turn IDs.

## What is changing

Make missing Copilot Agent Host model-call-to-turn correlation diagnosable without filling in guessed turn IDs.

Missing `turnId` currently conflates unknown sessions, unavailable active turns, expired correlation waits, and lifecycle/routing losses. This adds a small set of fields to the existing `copilotSdk/response.success` and `response.error` events; it adds no new event type, hashed identifier, or diagnostic retention cache.

For example, deleting a streaming session can now be identified as `waitExpired` with `ahSessionDisposedDuringWait = true`, rather than appearing as an unexplained missing turn.

Related to microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9110. This adds diagnostics; it does not fix the attribution loss or change the scorecard. The 100 ms deadline and existing turn-attribution behavior are preserved.

The generic forwarding path only dispatches by event kind. Session lookup, turn correlation, and diagnostics are isolated in `_forwardResponseTelemetry`; non-response events forward directly without reading turn-correlation state.

## Fields

- `ahCorrelationOutcome`: the host correlation decision, including a distinction between actual wait expiry and an already-forwarded short-circuit.
- `ahCorrelationWaitMs`: actual elapsed wait, only when a wait occurred.
- `ahActiveRootTurnIdAtResponse`: the active root turn captured at callback entry, only when final attribution is missing and a root turn was active.
- `ahSessionDisposedDuringWait`: whether the session was disposed by the end of the wait, only when a wait occurred and final attribution is missing.

`ahActiveRootTurnIdAtResponse` is contextual information, not an attribution repair. A subagent shares the root SDK session, and a late response may arrive during a different root turn. Do not coalesce this field into `turnId` or use it to assign model time to that turn.

Responses with a populated host `turnId` carry only the outcome and, where applicable, wait duration. Missing-attribution diagnostics apply to both `response.success` and `response.error`: a successful model response can still lack turn attribution. The fields distinguish failure categories but do not establish whether an unavailable completion was delayed, rejected, or never produced.

## Local runtime evidence

Exercised real OSS workflows with root tool loops, parallel subagents, cancellation/recovery, steering, and deletion near the final response.

- Normal delivery: 53 agent-initiated waits had a 4.10 ms median and 6.36 ms maximum, with no missing correlations.
- Lifecycle investigation reproduced a response arriving with a known session and active turn, followed by disposal 79.96 ms later. No completion callback was observed; the wait expired after 102.49 ms and forwarding omitted the turn.
- Before slimming the diagnostics to these fields, a subsequent run without temporary probes emitted `mappingWaited` at 4.50 ms for a normal response and `waitExpired` at 109.61 ms with the disposal flag set for a deleted streaming session. Successful response turn IDs matched host turn telemetry.

title: agentHost: Add macOS Docker PATH fallback
body:
## Summary

- Append `/usr/local/bin` to the Dev Container shell environment on macOS when absent, matching the existing Dev Containers workaround from microsoft/vscode-remote-release#5396.
- Apply the fallback after both successful shell resolution and timeout/error recovery, so Docker availability checks and container launches use the same corrected PATH.
- Preserve existing PATH precedence, avoid duplicate entries, handle empty/missing PATH without adding the current directory, and leave Linux/Windows unchanged.
- Copy the environment instead of modifying `process.env`; retain shell-resolution error logging and trace when the fallback is applied.

## Why

During a multi-window macOS startup, the shared-process shell probe can exceed the configured timeout. The inherited GUI environment may then contain only `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, so Docker installed under `/usr/local/bin` is not discovered and the New Session Dev Container checkbox disappears. A later shell result cannot recover the already-rejected cached promise.

This fixes Docker discovery independently of shell startup latency; it does not change shell timeouts, retry behavior, or feature gates.

title: git: detect corrupt index and provide recovery action
body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to VS Code! -->

### Why
On Windows, interrupted writes or process crashes (e.g. from background tasks or external tools) can truncate `.git/index` to 0 bytes. Git then fails with:
`fatal: .git/index: index file smaller than expected`

Previously, VS Code showed repeated blocking modal errors on commands, while background file-watcher refreshes failed silently without offering any way to recover.

### What
- **Error classification**: Added `GitErrorCodes.IndexCorrupted` matching corrupt/truncated index errors (`index file smaller than expected`, `index file corrupt`, `bad index file`, `error: bad signature`) in `git.ts`, `git.d.ts`, and `git.constants.ts`.
- **Transient retry**: Added a 3-attempt quadratic backoff retry in `Repository.updateModelState()` with an isolated cancellation token source, cancellation exit checks, and proper token disposal so in-flight external writes can finish without leaking stale updates.
- **Safe index rebuild**: Added `rebuildIndex()` which:
  - Validates `.git/index.lock` both prior to reset and before swapping to prevent collisions with active or concurrent Git processes.
  - Revalidates index health with `git status --porcelain` to preserve staged files if the index was already repaired.
  - Generates a unique temporary index path per attempt (`index.rebuild-${Date.now()}-${random}`) via `GIT_INDEX_FILE` so stale files from prior interrupted runs never block future recovery.
  - Atomically swaps in the replacement index via `fsPromises.rename` (cleaning up in `finally`), guaranteeing the repository is never stranded without an index if reset fails.
  - Safely handles unborn branches without `HEAD`.
- **Recovery action**: Shows a non-modal warning notification with a localized **Rebuild Index** button on both user commands and background watcher refreshes.
- **Target resolution**: Preserves the failing repository reference on errors so multi-root workspaces always rebuild the correct repository.
- **Unit tests**: Added classification tests for index corruption messages in `git.test.ts`.

### How to test
1. Open a Git repository in VS Code with some uncommitted changes.
2. Truncate `.git/index` to 0 bytes:
   ```sh
   > .git/index
   ```
3. Trigger a Git operation or wait for the background refresh:
   - A warning notification appears: *"The Git index file (.git/index) is corrupted. Would you like to rebuild it?"*
4. Click **Rebuild Index**:
   - The index is rebuilt cleanly.
   - Working tree changes remain intact and Git status returns to normal.

title: Acquire a process lock on the session data directory
body:
@deepak1556 

The main IPC handle is scoped to the product version, so right after an update the new process fails to detect the old one via claimInstance and both processes end up using the same user data directory at the same time. Chromium does not support sharing session data between multiple running browser processes and webview service worker registration then fails with an InvalidStateError.

Add a version independent process lock for the session data:

- createStaticIPCHandle now allows omitting the version so that the same handle is produced by all versions for a given user data directory (existing callers are unchanged)
- the main process serves that handle (environmentMainService. sessionDataLockHandle) for its whole lifetime before any storage in the user data directory is opened (claimSessionData runs right after claimInstance and before initServices)
- if a live lock holder exists, the process waits for it to exit (polling every second, dialog after 10s with Keep Waiting/Exit that re-appears every 60s), because concurrent use of the session data directory is unsupported and can corrupt Chromium state storage
- stale sockets of dead processes are recovered by probing the handle and unlinking it, mirroring claimInstance; the lock is released on shutdown

---

title: chat: allow collapsing queued chat requests
body:
Long queued prompts take up chat space without a way to collapse them. Add a keyboard-accessible chevron that collapses each queued or steering message into a single-line preview. Each message keeps its own expansion state across rendering updates, queue reordering, and the transition into the transcript. Collapsed messages are excluded from sticky-scroll headers.

The local queue processor preserves request identity. When steering messages merge, the combined prompt inherits an explicit collapse choice from any source message; users can then expand or collapse the combined prompt normally. The collapsed hover exposes the full preview, and Chat Accessibility Help documents the keyboard controls.

Fixes #326123.

Validation:

- Browser renderer suite: 70 passing, 1 pre-existing skipped test, including 13 collapse regressions covering independent state, keyboard interaction, both chat layouts, merged steering, attachment visibility, and full-preview hover text.
- ChatService suite: 101 passing, covering real queue/dequeue paths, merged steering identities, slash-command retries, and blocked troubleshoot requests.
- Client transpilation, scoped ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.

To test:

1. Start a chat request that keeps streaming, then add two long follow-up messages using **Add to Queue**.
2. Collapse the first queued message with its **Message** chevron. It should become a single-line preview while the second stays expanded.
3. Use Enter and Space on the toggle, then leave the first message collapsed. Scroll and resize the chat while the response streams; its state should remain unchanged.
4. Let the first queued message begin processing. It should stay collapsed, and expanding it should restore the complete prompt.

Runtime evidence:

[Watch the contributor's recording (MP4, 64 seconds)](https://github.com/LakshayKhattar/vscode/releases/download/pr-335208-runtime-evidence/queued-chat-collapse.mp4). At approximately 0:48, one queued prompt is collapsed while the other remains expanded; at 0:55, both are collapsed independently while the current response continues streaming. The original recording is hosted as an evidence asset on the contributor's fork.

The recording shows the disclosure UI at commit 53e40746. The dequeue and merged-steering fixes in 49af9453 are covered by the automated tests above.

title: update: detect Windows setup installs from product target
body:
Fixes #335000

Windows setup detection currently requires `unins000.exe` beside the executable. Inno Setup can legitimately generate a different numbered uninstaller, such as `unins001.exe`. This incorrectly classifies an official User Setup installation as an archive, selects the ZIP update feed, and opens the download in a browser instead of installing it.

- Detect Setup installations from the installer-generated `product.target` values `user` and `system`; missing or unexpected targets remain Archive.
- Use the same detection for update classification and both installer-mutex checks.
- Remove the filesystem probe and unnecessary process-global update-type cache.
- Add regression coverage for User/System Setup and missing or unexpected targets. Genuine ZIP installations retain manual updates.

title: Fix restored terminal icon when process attachment fails

title: fix: derive synced customization nonce from file content (build fix for vscode-engineering#3814)
body:
## Build failure

The Electron unit-test job failed on `main` with one deterministic failing test in `SyncedCustomizationBundler`:

```
1) SyncedCustomizationBundler
     bundles complete SKILL.md directories:
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected "actual" to be strictly unequal to: '737882158'
      at syncedCustomizationBundler.test.js:200:12
```

The assertion `assert.notStrictEqual(updatedResult!.ref.nonce, result.ref.nonce)` expects the bundle nonce to change after a reference file inside a skill directory is edited, but the recomputed nonce was identical. The two subsequent macOS-stage failures (non-production check and Publish Log Files, both reporting a missing `.build/logs`) are cascades of the test job aborting.

## Root cause

`SyncedCustomizationBundler._bundle` computed its change-detection nonce purely from file metadata:

```ts
entries.push({ ..., hashPart: `${hashKey}:${source.mtime}:${source.size}` });
```

The nonce therefore only reflects each file's `mtime` and `size`. When a file's content is edited to the same byte length within the filesystem's `mtime` resolution — as in the regression test, where `references/notes.md` changes from `reference content` (17 bytes) to `updated reference` (17 bytes) and the in-memory provider stamps both writes with the same `Date.now()` millisecond — the metadata is unchanged, so the nonce collides. The bundler then hits its "nothing changed" fast path and reuses the previous bundle, silently dropping the real content change from downstream agent-host syncs. This is a deterministic correctness bug, not a flake.

## How the fix works

The nonce is now derived from actual file content instead of metadata. File contents are read before the nonce is computed, and each file contributes a length-sensitive content hash (`hashBytes`) to the nonce inputs. A same-size content edit now produces a different hash, so the nonce changes and the bundle is correctly rewritten and re-synced. The metadata (`mtime`/`size`) is no longer part of the nonce. The write-skip optimization is preserved: the fast path still short-circuits when the content-based nonce is unchanged. Reading contents up front is not extra work — the previous code already read every file's contents immediately afterward to write the plugin tree; only the ordering relative to the nonce check moved.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Public culprit: `400640316376fbbdc6e901a7f5c23810bd5a9329` (#334568) added the regression test that exposes this pre-existing metadata-only nonce; the nonce logic itself predates it (introduced in #333827, `42b530c885a`). A reverting change would reintroduce the disposal-race log-noise fixes that #334568 also landed and would not correct the underlying content-insensitivity, so fix-forward is both safer and more complete. Owners to consult: `@pwang347`

## Validation

Could not run `npm ci`, the build, or the unit test in this environment (dependency install and node execution are blocked by the sandbox). The change is verified by source inspection: `hashBytes` iterates every content byte seeded with the length, so the two 17-byte reference-file variants in the failing test hash differently, making `updatedResult.ref.nonce !== result.ref.nonce` hold. TypeScript usage is consistent (`VSBuffer.buffer` is a `Uint8Array`; `numberHash` is exported from `base/common/hash`).

## Risk

Low and bounded. The change is confined to nonce derivation inside `SyncedCustomizationBundler`. Behavior is strictly more correct: the nonce now changes in more cases (content edits) and is stable across unrelated metadata churn (e.g. `mtime`-only touches no longer force a re-sync). No public API changes.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@pwang347`

title: Carry Chat Editor custom agent through first send
body:
Fixes #335176

## Summary

- carry the mode submitted from an untitled contributed Chat Editor into the real session model created by the first send
- apply the transfer only for the queued or accepted caller after pending-request arbitration, including late sends still addressed to the stale untitled URI
- add regression coverage for stale input state, custom submitted mode, concurrent senders with different modes, and late accepted sends

## Root cause

The Slack repro is a first-send handoff bug, not a custom-agent file/catalog deletion bug:

1. A fresh Chat Editor remembers and displays the real `Data` custom agent.
2. `ChatWidget` submits `hi` with the correct custom `modeInfo`.
3. `ChatService._materializeUntitledSession` creates and loads the real contributed-session model.
4. Materialization carries the untitled model's intended language model, but not its submitted chat mode.
5. The request runs with `Data`, while the real model swapped into the widget still has its default `Agent` mode.

The fix captures the actual submitted mode from `IChatSendRequestOptions.modeInfo` before materialization or stale-resource redirection. It applies that mode to the real model only when that caller is queued or accepted. The untitled input-model mode remains a fallback for programmatic requests that do not provide mode identity.

Applying after arbitration matters: concurrent first sends can materialize one real session but accept a different caller first. The accepted caller—not a rejected materialization owner—must determine the established picker. A later send still addressed to the stale untitled URI similarly transfers its own accepted mode.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- untitled contributed-session materialization suite: **11 passing**
- regression starts with stale `Agent` input state, submits custom `Data` mode information, and verifies the materialized real model stores `Data`
- concurrent regression submits different `Ask` and `Agent` modes and verifies the real model matches whichever request is accepted
- late-send regression submits a different mode through the stale untitled resource and verifies the established model follows the accepted late request
- falsification check: removing the transfer makes the custom-mode regression fail with an undefined real-model mode
- independent code review found no remaining issues
- real Code OSS verification using the VS Code repository's actual `Data` agent:
  - regular Chat Editor;
  - `Copilot` harness;
  - fresh session remembered `Data`;
  - sent `hi`;
  - picker remained `Data` continuously through materialization and active reasoning.

## Manual testing

1. Open the VS Code repository in an editor window.
2. Open **New Chat Editor**.
3. Verify the session harness is **Copilot**.
4. Select the real **Data** custom agent.
5. Send `hi`.
6. While the first request is reasoning and after it completes, verify the picker remains **Data** rather than resetting to **Agent**.
7. Click **New Chat Editor** and repeat the test; every fresh session should preserve Data through its first send.
8. After the first turn, switch between **Agent** and **Data** and send follow-ups to confirm explicit later selections still work.

## Evidence

### Before — exact Slack report and screenshots

https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C0AJZ5319PZ/p1788381749454329

### After — exact first-send flow

title: nes: fix: encode paths in inline suggestion requests
body:
> **Client-side workaround on hold.** This proposal changes the model-facing path representation. A prompt-preserving service-side cause has now been identified and is being validated instead. Do not merge this encoding change as the preferred root-cause fix.

Fixes #325491.

Related: #334759, #334523, #335001.

## Root cause

NES inserts file paths into unquoted, line-oriented prompt fields and diff-patch headers. Those paths were raw filesystem text. The Windows drive-letter fix in #333429 corrects workspace-relative path selection, but does not make the resulting path safe for the model protocol.

I reproduced the remaining failure on macOS in Code OSS with C# 2.140.9, without Unity Editor or C# Dev Kit. With `copilot-nes-lysithea-24`, the same C# source works under `Weekly-Material/Week-8` and fails under `Weekly Material/Week 8`. Adding a space to a plain C# filename also reproduces it. The separate completions panel still works.

The distinction is present in the incoming SSE choices, before client accumulation or patch parsing:

```text
Before, with the literal spaced path:
{"delta":{"content":""},"finish_reason":"stop"}

After, with an encoded path token:
{"delta":{"content":"Assets/Weekly%20Material/Week%208/Scripts/UnityProbe.cs:11\n"},"finish_reason":null}
```

The encoded request receives the subsequent deletion/addition chunks and produces ghost text. This is not a renderer change or a fallback to classic completions.

## Changes

- Percent-encode path segments in the shared prompt-path formatter. This covers the current file, recent/context files, edit history, and predicted output while preserving path separators and the previous Windows normalization.
- Resolve returned path tokens through one decode-once helper, shared by diff-patch targets and cross-file cursor jumps.
- Preserve literal percent sequences, filename delimiters, Unicode, and notebook-cell fragments. Reject malformed encoding explicitly rather than silently targeting a different file.
- Add regression coverage for serialization consistency, round trips, active-document progressive reveal, cross-file targets, malformed tokens, and cursor-target resolution.

No filesystem paths are renamed, no new setting is introduced, and unified NES remains the suggestions provider.

## Validation

- Focused Vitest suites: **430 passed; 4 Windows-only tests skipped on macOS**.
- Copilot extension TypeScript check passed.
- ESLint passed for all changed files.
- Live Code OSS before/after test, using the same profile and model configuration:
  - Before: spaced paths fail both automatic and explicit triggers; hyphenated control works.
  - After: **12/12 cases show ghost text**: automatic and explicit triggers for nested spaces, a hyphenated control, a filename space, literal `%20` plus a space, `#`/`?` delimiters, and a Unicode filename.
  - Successful items are from the NES provider, not classic completions.

The live test used the dev checkout and miscellaneous C# files in an MIT-licensed Unity sample, not a running Unity 6 project. It establishes the path-sensitive case, not that every related report has the same cause. Native Windows execution remains for CI.


## Before / after

Top: before the fix. Bottom: after the fix, on the same space-containing path. Cropped to the editor; both captures are from real OSS requests.

![Before and after: unified NES suggestions in the same C# file with spaces in its path](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61aa98ef-82c4-4777-a337-959641f78570)

## Summary

- makes the E2E test wait for the matching completion containing file-edit metadata; and

title: fix: resolve win32 product.json path in native policy smoke fixture (build fix for vscode-engineering#3813)
body:
## Build failure

The "Native Policy Plumbing" smoke tests (Electron, Windows) fail in their `before all` hook with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '...\VSCode-win32-x64\resources\app\product.json'`. Both Policy Plumbing tests throw before any assertion runs, failing the Windows Electron smoke stage on `main`.

## Root cause

`test/smoke/src/areas/policy/nativePolicy.ts` resolved the built product manifest on Windows by joining `resources/app/product.json` onto `path.dirname(getBuildElectronPath(options.codePath))` — effectively the root of the build output. However, the Windows built app nests its payload inside a subdirectory (e.g. `VSCode-win32-x64`). `getBuildElectronPath` itself accounts for this: for win32 it uses the `findFilePath` helper in `test/automation/src/electron.ts`, which searches one level of subdirectories for `resources/app/product.json`. The fixture bypassed that logic and assumed the file lived directly under the root, so `fs.readFileSync` hit a non-existent path and threw.

## How the fix works

Added an exported `getBuildProductPath(root)` helper in `test/automation/src/electron.ts` that resolves `product.json` per-platform, reusing the existing `findFilePath` subdirectory search on win32 (the same mechanism `getBuildElectronPath`/`getBuildVersion` already use). `nativePolicy.ts` now calls `getBuildProductPath(options.codePath)` instead of hand-rolling the path, so the Windows nested layout is handled correctly and darwin/linux behavior is preserved. This corrects the invalid path producer rather than guarding the consumer or swallowing the error.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.** Public culprit: PR microsoft/vscode#335107 (commit `644fe2ac`), which introduced the fixture. The regression is isolated to new test-fixture path resolution with no product/runtime/schema impact, and this fix-forward is a small, bounded correction that reuses existing, proven path-resolution logic. Reverting would only remove the new smoke coverage. Owners to consult: `@rwoll`

## Validation

Source inspection only. `getBuildElectronPath` (win32) and `getBuildVersion` (win32) already rely on `findFilePath` to locate `resources/app/product.json` within a subdirectory of the build root, confirming the nested layout; the new helper reuses the identical resolution. TypeScript type checking / smoke test execution could not be run in this environment (the `tsc` and build tooling were unavailable to the agent).

## Risk

Low. The change is confined to test automation/smoke code, adds a helper that mirrors existing behavior, and leaves the non-Windows paths functionally unchanged.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@rwoll`

title: Preserve established custom agent selection across catalog gaps
body:
Fixes #308525

## Summary

- keep an established Agent Host session's selected custom agent authoritative while its catalog hydrates
- restrict remembered-agent initialization to untitled sessions that do not already have an explicit selection
- cover first-send graduation, background completion, custom/default A/B switching, repeated close/reopen hydration, and remote Agent Host providers

## Root cause

`AgentHostAgentPickerContribution._initAgent` mixed two responsibilities:

1. seed a remembered agent into a new untitled session;
2. clear an established selection when the current custom-agent catalog did not contain its URI.

The second operation was unsafe. During first-send graduation, background hydration, close/reopen, and remote reconnects, the Agent Host can publish a non-empty but temporarily incomplete catalog. The picker interpreted that snapshot as permanent deletion and called `setAgent(undefined)`, clearing both the session facade and the remembered picker preference.

The fix limits `_initAgent` to its actual initialization role: an unselected untitled session may be seeded from the remembered preference; an established session is never mutated merely because a catalog snapshot does not currently resolve its selected URI. Explicitly choosing default `Agent` still clears the selection through the normal user-action path.

## Original repro coverage

| Reported scenario | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Custom agent changes to `Agent` during the first turn | The current provider already carries the picked agent onto the committed session. This PR prevents a partial committed-session catalog from immediately clearing it. Real-agent first-send verification passed. |
| Session completes while the user works in another session | The custom session remains authoritative while inactive. Real-agent background completion passed. |
| Switch between custom session A and default session B | Five real UI cycles passed: A remained custom and B remained `Agent`. The regression test also verifies the default session is never seeded from A. |
| Close and reopen the same session repeatedly | Five real close/reopen cycles passed. The picker model retains the selected ID during a catalog gap and emits a label refresh when the mode returns. |
| Remote Tunnel / SSH Agent Host | The same provider-neutral contribution handles local and `agenthost-*` providers. A remote provider-ID regression and the full remote provider suite pass. |
| Original Worktree video | The repository-to-worktree URI transition was separately fixed by #323548/#323566. Those changes carry the selection through graduation, rebase it to the worktree twin, and hydrate it from the draft. The existing worktree-rebase regression also passes. This PR adds the remaining protection against destructive partial-catalog cleanup. |
| `Mark as Done` / missing Changes panel content | Separate changes-state issue; not changed by this PR. |

The file-removal scenario used earlier is not required to reproduce the user flow. It is only a deterministic stress case for the same state boundary: a selected URI is temporarily absent while the catalog remains non-empty.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Agent Host picker, scoped mode-picker, and full remote provider suites: **92 passing**
- existing worktree custom-agent rebase regression: passing
- regression matrix covers:
  - untitled → committed graduation with a non-empty incomplete catalog;
  - completion while another default-Agent session is active;
  - repeated custom/default A/B switching;
  - three fresh-facade reopen/hydration cycles;
  - remote `agenthost-*` providers;
  - unchanged remembered-agent seeding for untitled sessions;
  - consumer-observed picker fallback and label recovery events.
- falsification check: restoring the pre-fix cleanup branch makes the graduation/reopen test clear the local selection four times and the remote test clear it once; the untitled initialization test still passes
- real Code OSS Agents Window using an authenticated Copilot Agent Host and a real workspace `.agent.md` file:
  - the first turn executed the custom instructions and returned `CUSTOM-308525`;
  - the picker recovered the custom label after graduation;
  - the custom session completed while a default session was active;
  - five A/B cycles preserved custom A and default B independently;
  - five close/reopen cycles restored the custom label and transcript markers.

## Manual testing

1. In a disposable workspace, add a real custom agent such as `.github/agents/persistence.agent.md`:

   ```md
   ---
   name: Persistence Agent
   description: Verifies custom-agent persistence.
   tools: [read]
   ---

   Read `marker.txt` before replying. End every response with exactly `CUSTOM-308525`.
   ```

2. Add `marker.txt`, open the **Agents Window**, select the workspace, choose **Copilot**, and select **Persistence Agent**.
3. Send `Read marker.txt and briefly confirm what it contains.`
4. Verify that after the session graduates and completes:
   - the picker returns to **Persistence Agent** if it briefly shows a hydration fallback;
   - the response ends with `CUSTOM-308525`.
5. Send another marker request, then immediately open a new session and leave it on default **Agent**. Let the custom session complete in the background.
6. Switch between the custom session and default session at least five times. Verify the custom session always shows **Persistence Agent** and the default session always shows **Agent**.
7. On the custom session, choose **More Actions... > Close**, then reopen it from the Sessions list. Repeat at least five times and verify the custom label and marker responses return each time.
8. Optional Worktree variant: use a Git workspace, enable **Worktree**, and repeat the first-send flow. Verify the custom agent remains selected after the workspace changes to the generated worktree.
9. Optional remote variant: repeat through a Tunnel or SSH Agent Host and verify the custom selection survives reconnect/reopen hydration.
10. Explicitly choose default **Agent** on a session and verify it remains default; the fix must not restore a custom agent after an intentional user change.

### Optional deterministic stress case

Temporarily make only the selected `.agent.md` unavailable while another custom agent remains in the catalog, then restore it. The picker may show `Agent` while unavailable, but it must recover the original custom label after discovery catches up.

title: chat: avoid watching Copilot CLI plugin contents
body:
Fixes #334391

## What was happening

Shared plugin discovery watches each plugin root and its manifest and component paths (`commands`, `skills`, `agents`, `hooks`, and so on). These watchers make in-place edits show up immediately, but for Copilot CLI-installed plugins they leave `ReadDirectoryChangesW` handles inside CLI-owned directories. Windows then prevents the CLI from renaming or deleting those directories during an atomic install, update, or uninstall, resulting in `Access is denied`.

## Why content watchers can be skipped here

CLI-installed plugin directories are managed snapshots: the supported update path replaces the whole plugin directory rather than editing its contents in place. CLI discovery already watches the `installed-plugins` ancestors and each marketplace bucket, which is enough to observe those directory swaps. On a bucket change, this fix rebuilds the CLI plugin entry instead of reusing its cached contents, so the replacement still appears without a reload. Hidden transaction directories are ignored, while other plugin discovery sources retain their existing content watchers for live in-place edits.

## Verification

- Reproduced before the fix in a full Code OSS window on Windows: after opening Agent Customizations and confirming the fixture plugin was discovered, renaming its installed plugin root failed with `Access to the path ... is denied`; the same rename succeeded before launch and after closing Code OSS.
- Verified the fix in a freshly rebuilt full Code OSS window: renamed the installed plugin to a hidden sibling, created its replacement at the original path, and deleted the old directory while Code OSS remained open. All operations succeeded, and Agent Customizations automatically changed from `VS Code 334391 Repro` to `VS Code 334391 Replacement` without a reload.
- Added focused coverage for excluding hidden transaction directories, avoiding watchers at or below CLI plugin roots, and rebuilding replacement plugin contents.
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Targeted ESLint for the changed TypeScript files
- `scripts\test.bat --grep "AgentPlugin format detection"` (48 passing)

title: nes: fix: preserve viewport when accepting multi-line edits
body:
cc @hediet

## Summary

Preserve the editor viewport when accepting a multi-line next edit suggestion (NES).

Multi-line NES rendering uses a view zone to reserve space before the suggested lines exist in the model. Acceptance inserts real lines and then removes that redundant zone, so removal must not apply the compensation used for ordinary dismissal.

## Root cause

The acceptance guard in `AdditionalLinesWidget` still checked the legacy edit source `inlineSuggestion.accept`.

Inline completion acceptance now reaches `CodeEditorWidget.onBeforeExecuteEdit` as the typed source `inlineCompletionAccept`. The stale comparison never matched, so acceptance was treated like dismissal and `keepCursorStable` subtracted the removed zone height from `scrollTop`.

For a seven-line suggestion, this moved the viewport upward by exactly seven lines.

## Fix

Recognize `inlineCompletionAccept` when suppressing view-zone removal compensation.

This restores the intended acceptance behavior while retaining compensation for non-accept dismissal.

## Regression coverage

The new browser tests use a real, laid-out `CodeEditorWidget` and the production `InlineEditsInsertionView`:

- accepting a seven-line insertion preserves both `scrollTop` and a stable screen-space anchor;
- dismissing the same insertion after moving the cursor below it still compensates and preserves the cursor's screen-space position.

## Validation

- Targeted Electron browser tests: 3 passing
- ESLint on both changed files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Real Code OSS before/after scenarios: baseline jumps from line 75 to 68; fixed build remains at line 75

## Before / after

**Before — acceptance jumps upward by seven lines**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ba3187d-8870-4ad7-96b7-a5ea9807290c

**After — acceptance preserves the viewport anchor**

title: agentHost: only remove worktree on archive when in sync with remote
body:
## Summary

Tightens the safety policy for automatic worktree removal on session archive. Previously `_cleanupWorktreeOnArchive` in `worktreeIsolation.ts` committed any uncommitted changes and then removed the worktree, relying on branch preservation for reversibility. This changes the gate so the worktree is **only removed when git is fully up to date with its remote**:

- the branch tracks an upstream branch,
- there are no unpushed commits (`outgoingChanges === 0`), and
- the working tree is clean (`uncommittedChanges === 0`).

The new `_isBranchUpToDateWithRemote` helper **fails closed** — if the git state can't be determined, the branch has no upstream, or there is any local-only work, the worktree is left intact so nothing is ever discarded. The existing checks (worktree already gone, branch missing) and the reversible unarchive-recreate flow are unchanged.

## Why

Auto-removal should never risk losing local-only work. Requiring the branch to be in sync with the remote is a stronger, easier-to-reason-about guarantee than committing-then-removing, and it matches the intent that removal is a safe, reversible disk-space optimization.

## Testing

- New test: `cleanup on archive keeps the worktree when the branch is not up to date with its remote` — covers no-upstream, unpushed commits, uncommitted changes, and unknown git state.
- Existing `cleanup on archive removes a clean worktree and unarchive recreates it` still passes.
- Full `WorktreeIsolation` suite: 41 passing.
- ESLint clean on changed files.

## Notes for reviewers

This is intentionally independent of the auto-archive/auto-delete settings work in #334341; that PR's only worktree change is the delete-time `canAutomaticallyDeleteArchivedSession` gate and does not touch `_cleanupWorktreeOnArchive`.

title: fix: center the fork glyph in the chat checkpoint toolbar
body: Fixes #335071 ### Problem The fork button's glyph sits about 2px left of center, leaving a visible gap along its right edge. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | ### Cause `ChatForkActionViewItem` renders the glyph inside a nested `.chat-fork-action-icon` span. The shared actionbar rule (`actionbar.css`) sizes any descendant codicon to a 16x16 flex box and centers it vertically, but never horizontally. The checkpoint toolbar renders this icon at the **compact 12px** size, so the glyph was left-aligned inside a 16px box and the unused 4px landed on the right. The button's own padding was already symmetric, so the offset came entirely from the inner box. ### Fix One scoped declaration in `chat.css`, added to the fork-label rule that already exists in the checkpoint block: ```css .chat-fork-action-icon { justify-content: center; } ``` Deliberately unchanged: button size, padding, divider lines, separator dot, **Restore Checkpoint** placement, tooltip, focus ring, and the ARIA busy/label handling. No `!important`, no positional offsets, no `:has()`, and no change to the global actionbar styling that other toolbars rely on. Both the chat view and the Agents Window go through the shared `ChatForkActionViewItem`, so no window-specific override is needed. ### Tests Extended `chatForkActionViewItem.test.ts` to render the view item inside a production-shaped checkpoint toolbar hierarchy against the real stylesheet, asserting centered alignment and unchanged button dimensions across **idle -> running -> completed**. The compact loading spinner reuses the same span, so the running state is covered too. The existing spinner and accessibility assertions are preserved. ### Verification - The regression test fails on the pre-fix CSS (`glyphAlignment: 'normal'` in all three states) and passes with the fix - `chatForkActionViewItem` and `chatRestoreCheckpointActionViewItem` suites pass - `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css` passes - Measured the real glyph pseudo-element over CDP in a running build: horizontal offset moved from **-1.999px to -0.003px** in both the chat view and the Agents Window, with button width and height unchanged
